1	const std = @import("std");
     2	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
     3	const renderer = @import("../renderer.zig");
     4	const terminal = @import("../terminal/main.zig");
     5	const termio = @import("../termio.zig");
     6	const MessageData = @import("../datastruct/main.zig").MessageData;
     7	
     8	/// The messages that can be sent to an IO thread.
     9	///
    10	/// This is not a tiny structure (~40 bytes at the time of writing this comment),
    11	/// but the number of messages we send to the IO thread is also very small.
    12	/// At the current size we can queue 26,000 messages before consuming a MB of RAM.
    13	pub const Message = union(enum) {
    14	    /// Represents a write request. Magic number comes from the largest
    15	    /// other union value. It can be upped if we add a larger union member
    16	    /// in the future.
    17	    pub const WriteReq = MessageData(u8, 38);
    18	
    19	    /// Request a color scheme report is sent to the PTY.
    20	    color_scheme_report: struct {
    21	        /// Force write the current color scheme
    22	        force: bool,
    23	    },
    24	
    25	    /// Request a visibility report is sent to the PTY.
    26	    visibility_report: struct {
    27	        /// The visibility state to report.
    28	        visible: bool,
    29	
    30	        /// Send the report even when mode 2033 is disabled.
    31	        force: bool,
    32	    },
    33	
    34	    /// Purposely crash the renderer. This is used for testing and debugging.
    35	    /// See the "crash" binding action.
    36	    crash: void,
    37	
    38	    /// The derived configuration to update the implementation with. This
    39	    /// is allocated via the allocator and is expected to be freed when done.
    40	    change_config: struct {
    41	        alloc: Allocator,
    42	        ptr: *termio.Termio.DerivedConfig,
    43	    },
    44	
    45	    /// Activate or deactivate the inspector.
    46	    inspector: bool,
    47	
    48	    /// Resize the window.
    49	    resize: renderer.Size,
    50	
    51	    /// Request a size report is sent to the PTY ([in-band
    52	    /// size report, mode 2048](https://gist.github.com/rockorager/e695fb2924d36b2bcf1fff4a3704bd83) and
    53	    /// [XTWINOPS](https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h4-Functions-using-CSI-_-ordered-by-the-final-character-lparen-s-rparen:CSI-Ps;Ps;Ps-t.1EB0)).
    54	    size_report: SizeReport,
    55	
    56	    /// Clear the screen.
    57	    clear_screen: struct {
    58	        /// Include clearing the history
    59	        history: bool,
    60	    },
    61	
    62	    /// Scroll the viewport
    63	    scroll_viewport: terminal.Terminal.ScrollViewport,
    64	
    65	    /// Selection scrolling. If this is set to true then the termio
    66	    /// thread starts a timer that will trigger a `selection_scroll_tick`
    67	    /// message back to the surface. This ping/pong is because the
    68	    /// surface thread doesn't have access to an event loop from libghostty.
    69	    selection_scroll: bool,
    70	
    71	    /// Jump forward/backward n prompts.
    72	    jump_to_prompt: isize,
    73	
    74	    /// Send this when a synchronized output mode is started. This will
    75	    /// start the timer so that the output mode is disabled after a
    76	    /// period of time so that a bad actor can't hang the terminal.
    77	    start_synchronized_output: void,
    78	
    79	    /// Enable or disable linefeed mode (mode 20).
    80	    linefeed_mode: bool,
    81	
    82	    /// The surface gained or lost focus.
    83	    focused: bool,
    84	
    85	    /// Record a Kitty clipboard protocol session grant for a password
    86	    /// so future requests carrying it skip the permission prompt, for
    87	    /// reads and writes respectively.
    88	    kitty_clipboard_grant_read: KittyClipboardGrant,
    89	    kitty_clipboard_grant_write: KittyClipboardGrant,
    90	
    91	    /// Write where the data fits in the union.
    92	    write_small: WriteReq.Small,
    93	
    94	    /// Write where the data pointer is stable.
    95	    write_stable: WriteReq.Stable,
    96	
    97	    /// Write where the data is allocated and must be freed.
    98	    write_alloc: WriteReq.Alloc,
    99	
   100	    /// The payload of the kitty_clipboard_grant_* messages. The
   101	    /// password is allocated and must be freed.
   102	    pub const KittyClipboardGrant = struct {
   103	        alloc: Allocator,
   104	        pw: []const u8,
   105	    };
   106	
   107	    /// Return a write request for the given data. This will use
   108	    /// write_small if it fits or write_alloc otherwise. This should NOT
   109	    /// be used for stable pointers which can be manually set to write_stable.
   110	    pub fn writeReq(alloc: Allocator, data: anytype) !Message {
   111	        return switch (try WriteReq.init(alloc, data)) {
   112	            .stable => unreachable,
   113	            .small => |v| Message{ .write_small = v },
   114	            .alloc => |v| Message{ .write_alloc = v },
   115	        };
   116	    }
   117	
   118	    /// Free resources owned by a message that will not be processed.
   119	    /// The message is invalid after this call.
   120	    pub fn deinit(self: *const Message) void {
   121	        switch (self.*) {
